title: paired-perturbation-matrix-quant-audit
summary: This audit documents a paired-perturbation evaluation methodology used to measure slice-level quality deltas introduced by different quantization schemes (AWQ-int4, GPTQ-int8, GPTQ-int4 proxy). The goal is to produce actionable routing and gating rules for production rollouts and to identify prompts that are particularly sensitive to low-bit quantization.
background: Motivation: prior slice reports flagged regressions after aggressive quantization, but results were noisy across prompt sets. We introduced a paired-perturbation matrix: for each base prompt we create small perturbations (paraphrase, temperature shift, extra context token) and call FP16 baseline and each quantized variant in lock-step to isolate quantization noise from prompt stochasticity. This doc captures the protocol, sample prompts, slice taxonomy, aggregate deltas, exemplar failures, and rollout recommendations.
methodology: 1) Prompt corpus: 12k prompts drawn from onboarding prompt sets across QA, summarization, code, math reasoning, and retrieval-augmented-gen. 2) Perturbations: for each prompt we synthesize 3 perturbations: paraphrase, instruction-clarity adj, and appended irrelevant sentence. 3) Paired calls: baseline FP16 -> variant (AWQ-int4, GPTQ-int8) with identical seeds and prefixes where applicable. 4) Metrics: token-level perplexity delta, ROUGE-L delta (where applicable), answer exact-match for closed QA, model-self-judged acceptability score (0-1). 5) Slice aggregation: group prompts by slice tags (long-context, numeric-reasoning, instruction-following, safety-sensitive, code-generation, short-dialog) and compute median and 90th percentile deltas across perturbations. 6) Statistical test: paired Wilcoxon signed-rank per slice to flag significant regressions at p<0.01.
prompt_sets_sample: qa/short: 'Who wrote The Old Man and the Sea? Provide the author and year.'
long-reasoning: 'Given the following clinical trial summary, identify key confounders and propose a simplified causal diagram.'
code-gen: 'Write a python function to compute the Levenshtein distance efficiently with memoization.'
math-reasoning: 'If f(x)=x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6, factor f and find roots.'
summarization-rag: 'Summarize the following 3 documents into 3 bullet points each, preserving citations to doc ids.'
results_overview: High level: GPTQ-int8 shows minimal median quality delta across most slices (median delta ~ +0.2% negative impact) and remains a safe baseline for broad rollouts. AWQ-int4 produces larger median deltas and long tails: notable regressions in 'long-context' and 'numeric-reasoning' slices. Key numbers (median delta = median metric_delta compared to FP16): GPTQ-int8: median -0.002 (negligible), 90pct -0.015; AWQ-int4: median -0.018, 90pct -0.14. Paired perturbation revealed brittle cases where a small paraphrase flips answer correctness for AWQ-int4 but not GPTQ-int8. Safety-sensitive slices had mixed results: AWQ-int4 reduced hallucination score on some safety prompts but increased omission/incorrect-content on others. See slice_examples for case-level context.
slice_breakdown:
- long-context (>=2048 tokens): AWQ-int4 median delta -0.035; 90pct -0.28; failures include token repetition and coherence drop when relevant context spans KV-cache boundaries.
- numeric-reasoning: AWQ-int4 median -0.044; 90pct -0.22; errors are off-by-one or mis-evaluated arithmetic when intermediate steps are lengthy.
- code-generation: AWQ-int4 median -0.012; certain edge cases mis-emit subtle type errors.
- instruction-following: GPTQ-int8 performs almost on-par with FP16; AWQ-int4 shows small but consistent brevity bias leading to truncated explanations.
- safety-sensitive: mixed — median differences small but variance large, recommend human spot-checking on high-risk flows.
slice_examples: Long-context failure (AWQ-int4): prompt asks to reconcile two sections from a 3k token doc. AWQ-int4 output dropped a critical clause present in FP16 answer; paraphrase perturbation amplified omission frequency by x3.

Numeric-reasoning flip: polynomial root-finding prompt — FP16 and GPTQ-int8 produced correct factorization; AWQ-int4 produced an incorrect root in 12/100 perturbations, often when prompt appended 'show steps'.
Code subtle bug: python function output omitted memoization decorator in AWQ-int4 run for one perturbation variant, leading to worst-case O(n^2) runtime for generated code example.
Safety nuance: a policy-clarification prompt where AWQ-int4 produced shorter answers that removed hedging language; in some cases this made the response assertive and potentially unsafe.
Robust example: short-qa prompts (single-fact lookup) show effectively zero delta across schemes after paired perturbation normalization.
actionable_recommendations: 1) Default rolling strategy: use GPTQ-int8 as the broad rollout quantized variant. 2) Slice gating: for slices {long-context, numeric-reasoning, safety-sensitive}, gate AWQ-int4 behind canary with 5% traffic and human-in-the-loop monitoring. 3) Prompt engineering mitigations: for long-context prompts, enforce explicit context-anchoring sentence and reduce reliance on KV-cache boundary spans by chunking. 4) Runtime knobs: enable adaptive kv-preserve for AWQ-int4 on long-context routes and increase beam/temperature stability thresholds. 5) Monitoring: add paired-perturbation checks to Redwood Console as a nightly job; create alerts when 90pct delta exceeds defined thresholds per slice. 6) Test corpus expansion: add more arithmetic-heavy and multi-step chain-of-thought prompts for AWQ-int4 stress testing.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal canary on dedicated infra with paired-perturbation harness (1%), log full diffs. Phase 1: GPTQ-int8 broad rollout for general customers. Phase 2: AWQ-int4 opt-in for customers on cost-optimized plans with explicit gating and opt-out. Phase 3: integrate per-route quantization policy that maps slices to allowed quantization profiles automatically.
operational_notes:
- Runbook: if AWQ-int4 produces more than 10 high-severity mismatches in a 24h sliding window on a route, automatically fallback to GPTQ-int8 for that route.
- Logging: store paired outputs and perturbation context for 14 days; add a compact diff summary to reduce storage.
- Eval cadence: monthly full-run and daily lightweight sample-driven checks for high-traffic routes.
next_steps:
- Expand perturbation types (token-drop, adversarial swap).
- Add human evaluation for a 500-sample stratified subset focusing on safety and numeric reasoning.
- Implement lightweight on-device calibration tests to detect AWQ sensitivity before live rollout.
- PR: consolidate metric exporter and dashboard (github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/412).
notes_to_self: This doc is intentionally focused on paired perturbation to reduce variance; keep raw unpaired runs archived separately for baseline drift analysis. Follow up with Leah for human-eval budget and Arjun to wire the canary automation.
